name: The Corridor of the Three Vows

exhibits.title: The Vicereg Twins
exhibits.text: Three sisters carved in one block of pale stone — the Vicereg Twins, despite the inconvenient arithmetic of their name. The first holds a tuning fork (Invariance), the second a wide brass fan (Variance), the third a many-stringed lyre (Covariance). This is VICReg — Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization (Bardes, Ponce and LeCun, ICLR 2022) — a self-supervised loss that prevents collapse with no negative pairs and no asymmetric scribes at all: three explicit vows, sworn over every batch of embeddings, whose only mutual satisfaction is a representation that is semantically tight, globally spread, and dimensionally rich.

exhibits.title: The Three Vows
exhibits.text: INVARIANCE (the tuning fork): two glimpses of the same thing must sound the same note — a mean-squared-error term pulling the embeddings of two augmented views of one image together. VARIANCE (the brass fan): no collapsing onto a single note — a hinge penalty keeps the standard deviation of EACH embedding dimension, computed across the batch, at no less than one. COVARIANCE (the lyre): no string may merely echo another — the off-diagonal entries of the embedding covariance matrix are driven toward zero, so the spread that Variance wins is not secretly crowded into one direction. The vows pull against each other; their joint solution is the useful representation.

exhibits.title: The Expander h-phi
exhibits.text: Before the sisters stands a glass funnel that EXPANDS each voice into a far larger choir before the vows are heard. Two purposes. First: the Expander does the discarding FOR the encoder. Invariance would force a singer to forget anything that varies between two glimpses; the Expander is downstream and absorbs that demand, so the encoder's own representation stays rich. Second: in a small space, two pitches can be uncorrelated yet secretly dependent (one the square of the other). Expanded into higher dimensions, such nonlinear dependencies bloom into LINEAR correlations along new axes — where the Covariance vow can finally hear and silence them. After training, the funnel is politely dismissed; only the encoder walks onward.

exhibits.title: Song of the Three Vows
exhibits.caption: VICReg: two augmented views, a shared encoder, the Expander h-phi, and three loss terms applied to the expanded embeddings.

exhibits.title: The Headmistress of Charms
exhibits.subtitle: On the purpose of the glass funnel
exhibits.text: The vows of the sisters are demanding, child — Invariance in particular would force a singer to forget anything that varied between two glimpses of the same thing. If the singer herself had to do the forgetting, she would walk out of this corridor poorer than she walked in. So the Expander stands between her and the sisters. It is downstream. It absorbs the demand. And mark this also: in a small space two voices can be uncorrelated yet still secretly bound — a pitch that always equals the square of another will fool any linear ear. Expand the choir into higher dimensions and the hidden dependencies bloom into plain correlations, where Covariance can silence them. That is why the funnel exists, and why we dismiss it when the training is done.

exhibits.title: Chapter 2: The Three Vows of the Vicereg Twins
exhibits.text:
Across the castle, in a sunlit corridor of the Charms Department, hung three portraits that no first-year ever quite understood. They depicted three sisters — the Vicereg Twins, despite the inconvenient arithmetic of their name — and each sister carried a different instrument: a tuning fork, a wide brass fan, and a many-stringed lyre.

The sisters had taken three vows together, long before they entered the portraits, and the vows were spoken every morning when the sun struck the corridor at the proper angle.

The first sister, who held the tuning fork, was Invariance. Her vow was the simplest: *two glimpses of the same thing must sound the same note*. When a student walked past her in a red cloak, and again later in the same cloak with a slightly different hood drawn up, her tuning fork would chime once for the first glimpse and once for the second, and the two chimes had to match. The pull of her vow brought related things together.

The second sister, who held the brass fan, was Variance. Her vow stood in open rebellion against her sister's. *No two students may sound alike across the whole batch of arrivals*, she insisted. She would fan her instrument until each dimension of every chime held its own breadth — a standard deviation no smaller than one, in the units of the corridor. If everyone collapsed onto a single note, she would push them apart again. She was, the older students said, the reason the corridor never fell silent.

The third sister, who held the many-stringed lyre, was Covariance. Her vow was the subtlest. *No string may merely echo another*, she said. She tuned the lyre so that each string carried its own independent voice, penalizing any off-diagonal whisper of correlation between them. Without her, all the spread that Variance produced would crowd into a single direction, and the corridor would seem wide but in fact be flat.

To a passerby, the three vows seemed to contradict one another. Invariance pulled things together. Variance pushed them apart. Covariance forced them outward along every axis at once. And yet — and this was the magic of the corridor — there existed a single configuration of song in which all three sisters were satisfied: a representation that was semantically tight, globally spread, and dimensionally rich. The students who learned to sing in this configuration were said to walk out of the corridor with a deeper hearing than they had walked in with [[ref:bardes2022]].

Before the sisters' instruments, however, stood a peculiar contraption: a glass funnel that took each student's voice and *expanded* it into a far larger choir before the three sisters ever heard it. This was the Expander, hφ, and it had two purposes that the headmistress of Charms had once explained at length to a confused class of fourth-years.

"First," she had said, pacing before the funnel, "the Expander does the discarding *for* the encoder. The vows of the sisters are demanding — Invariance in particular would force a singer to forget anything that varied between two glimpses of the same thing. If the singer herself had to do the forgetting, she would walk out of the corridor poorer than she walked in. But the Expander stands between her and the sisters. It is downstream. It absorbs the demand. The singer's own voice remains rich; only the Expander's voice is flattened.

"Second," she continued, tapping the glass, "in a small space, two voices can be uncorrelated yet still secretly dependent. Imagine a pitch that always equals the *square* of another pitch — they will appear uncorrelated to any linear ear, yet they are bound. Expand the choir into higher dimensions, however, and these nonlinear dependencies bloom into linear correlations along new axes, where Covariance can finally hear them and silence them. The Expander makes the hidden dependencies visible, so that decorrelation can do its work."

After the training of each student was complete, the Expander was politely dismissed. Only the encoder — the singer herself — walked onward into the rest of the school. The funnel had served its purpose: a soft buffer between the singer and the sisters, a place for the bruising work of vow-keeping to land.

exhibits.title: VICReg: the three vows over a batch of embeddings
exhibits.caption: The three loss terms of VICReg (Bardes, Ponce & LeCun, ICLR 2022), read left to right. INVARIANCE: two augmented views of one image are encoded and expanded into embeddings z and z', and a mean-squared-error term pulls the pair together — relatedness becomes proximity. VARIANCE: across a whole batch, the standard deviation of each embedding dimension is kept at or above a hinge target of 1.0 via the penalty max(0, 1 - std); the short, penalized dimensions are pushed back up to the line, so no dimension collapses to a constant. COVARIANCE: the embedding covariance matrix is decorrelated — off-diagonal entries are driven toward zero (before vs after), so the spread that Variance wins is not secretly crowded into a few correlated directions. The three vows pull against one another; their joint solution is a representation that is semantically tight, globally spread, and dimensionally rich — collapse-free with no negative pairs.

exhibits.title: The Expander h-phi: a discardable buffer that takes the loss
exhibits.caption: Where the loss actually lands. An image view passes through the encoder f-theta, producing a representation y of dimension d, then through the Expander h-phi, producing an embedding z of much higher dimension D >> d, on which the three VICReg terms are computed. The expander earns its keep twice. First, it absorbs the invariance pressure: since the loss is applied downstream of the encoder, the encoder's own output y need not forget whatever differs between two views of the same image, so it stays rich. Second, raising the dimension turns nonlinear correlations into linear ones along new axes, which the covariance term can then remove — decorrelation can only silence what it can linearly hear. After training the expander is discarded; only the encoder f-theta walks onward into downstream tasks.
